summary: T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951) and was Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras.

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later serving there as Professor (~1953–1967), alongside appointments at Oxford (~1949–1950) and McMaster University (attested 1982).
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Madras, where he is attested in 1994 and as a professor in 2008.

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He was affiliated with Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972), where he served as a professor (attested 1984–1992).

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).
T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (born 1933) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held a post at Osmania University (~1959–1968) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (~1968–1994).

T. Venkatacharya was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente and at the University of Toronto, where he was a professor in the Department of East Asian Studies (attested 1971).

Tadao Yoshikawa (born 1937) is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1955–1965). He held posts at Hanazono University (~1966–1974), Kyoto University (professor ~1983–2000), and Ryukoku University (professor ~2000–2007).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Nara University and held posts at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tadashi Tani (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yuichi Kajiyama and completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University. He was a professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000) and later lectured at several universities.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London by 1978. He served at SOAS University of London as Professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader in the Department of the Study of Religions (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.
Taido Kitamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Shuchiin University, including as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later from attested 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton (born 1950) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Graduate Theological Union (~1990–1998) and studied under multiple traditional teachers. He has taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994) and Loyola University Chicago (~2008).

Taiji Kuroda (born 1952) specializes in Indology and philosophy, completing doctoral credits at Kyoto University in 1976. He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1986) and Osaka Gakuin College (attested 1988).

Taijun Inokuchi (1930–2007) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and served as representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He held posts at Japan Women's University and the University of Tokyo.

Taiken Kyuma (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as an Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He held an assistant professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
